q: A drug blocks the final step of RuBP regeneration (phosphorylation of ribulose phosphate by ATP) in illuminated chloroplasts. What happens?
options: RuBP and GP both accumulate, because RuBP can no longer be used up by Rubisco
Carbon fixation speeds up, because all of the ATP saved can now be used to make more TP
Ribulose phosphate builds up, RuBP falls, and carbon fixation and TP export decline
NADPH production by PSI stops immediately, because ATP is no longer needed
explanation: The final regeneration step uses ATP to phosphorylate ribulose phosphate into RuBP. Blocking it makes its substrate build up and RuBP fall; with less CO2 acceptor, Rubisco fixes less carbon, so GP, TP and sugar production decline. NADPH is made until NADP+ runs out (less is reoxidised in the Calvin cycle), after which the light reactions slow too.
